traceability.evidence: Story file exists: docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md,Rule implementation: src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts implements the migration logic for legacy @story/@req to @supports, with detailed handling for detection, multi-story cases, and conservative auto-fix (functions analyzeComment, hasMultipleStories, collectStoryAndReqMetadata, buildImplementsAutoFix, applyImplementsReplacement, processComment).,Rule naming and alias wiring: src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES includes "prefer-implements-annotation". - A dedicated block (annotated with @supports ... REQ-RULE-NAME) creates a primary rule entry rules["prefer-supports-annotation"] that reuses the prefer-implements-annotation implementation but with meta.deprecated=false. - The original rules["prefer-implements-annotation"] is marked deprecated, with meta.replacedBy = ["prefer-supports-annotation"]. - This satisfies REQ-RULE-NAME and the acceptance criterion "Rule Naming" (primary name prefer-supports-annotation, alias prefer-implements-annotation deprecated).,Unit tests for this story: tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts - Header explicitly ties tests to this story and requirements: * @story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md * @req REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY. - First describe block: "prefer-supports-annotation / prefer-implements-annotation aliasing (Story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS)". * Runs RuleTester for both rule names: "prefer-implements-annotation" and "prefer-supports-annotation" against the same valid/invalid cases, proving the alias + primary naming both work. * Valid cases ([REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION]) assert that comments with only @story, only @req, only @supports, or mixed @story/@supports or @req/@supports (without both @story and @req) are all ignored, satisfying REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION and "Both Formats Valid" when rule is enabled. * Invalid cases cover: - [REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING] single-story @story + @req producing messageId "preferImplements" and an auto-fix output converting to @supports. - [REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT] mixed @story/@req + @supports producing messageId "cannotAutoFix" with a reason string, and no output transform. - [REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT] multiple @story paths in same block producing messageId "multiStoryDetected". - [REQ-AUTO-FIX] simple single @story + single @req auto-fixing to one @supports line. - [REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX] single @story with multiple @req lines auto-fixing to one @supports line containing all REQ IDs. - [REQ-AUTO-FIX] complex @req or complex @story content producing warnings (preferImplements) but no auto-fix (no output specified), verifying the conservative auto-fix strategy and REQ-VALID-OUTPUT/REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT (no risky transformations).,Configuration / severity tests: tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts second describe block - "prefer-implements-annotation configuration severity (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY)". - Verifies the rule is disabled by default (not present) in both configs.recommended and configs.strict from src/index.ts, satisfying the acceptance criteria "Optional Warning" (default off) and "Configurable Enforcement" default off. - Verifies that flat config objects can specify both "traceability/prefer-implements-annotation" and "traceability/prefer-supports-annotation" with severities "warn" or "error" (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, and alias behavior).,Rule behavior & auto-fix implementation details: src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts - Detection and messaging: * analyzeComment() and processComment() implement REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING and REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT by: - Requiring both hasStory and hasReq for any action. - If a comment also has @supports, reporting messageId "cannotAutoFix" with reason "comment mixes @story/@req with existing @supports annotations". - If multiple story paths are detected (hasMultipleStories(storyPaths) where storyPaths.size > MULTI_STORY_THRESHOLD), reporting messageId "multiStoryDetected". - Otherwise reporting "preferImplements", optionally with a fix if buildImplementsAutoFix returns one. - Auto-fix (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT): * collectStoryAndReqMetadata() parses comment lines (normalized via normalizeCommentLine) and collects: - storyLineIndices, reqLineIndices, reqIds, and a single storyPath. - It only accepts simple forms: "@story " and "@req " with exactly two tokens; any more tokens marks storyPath null to force bail-out (no fix), satisfying REQ-VALID-OUTPUT (avoid ambiguous forms) and examples in the story. * buildImplementsAutoFix() requires: - Exactly one distinct story path (storyPaths.size === 1), - Exactly one @story line index, - At least one @req line index, - Non-null storyPath. Otherwise returns null, so only safe single-story, simple patterns are auto-fixed (REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT). * applyImplementsReplacement() constructs a single "@supports ..." line with preserved indentation and prefix (via regex ^(\s*\*?\s*)) and replaces the original @story line, removing @req lines, leaving all other lines untouched. This maintains JSDoc structure and order (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, acceptance criterion "Preserve Order"). * meta.fixable is set to "code" and context.report in processComment provides fix when available, enabling ESLint --fix integration (REQ-AUTO-FIX). - Backward compatibility (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION): * When the rule is disabled (default severity "off" in configs and user config), ESLint never invokes create(), so no additional diagnostics are emitted; legacy @story/@req validation remains solely under other rules (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, valid-annotation-format, etc.). * Even when the rule is enabled, it intentionally ignores comments that contain only @story, only @req, or only @supports (as verified in valid RuleTester cases).,Plugin export wiring: src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES lists "prefer-implements-annotation"; dynamic loader fills rules["prefer-implements-annotation"]. - A dedicated block then: * Creates rules["prefer-supports-annotation"] as a clone of that implementation with meta.deprecated = false, ensuring the canonical rule name exists and uses the same behavior. * Marks meta.deprecated = true and meta.replacedBy = ["prefer-supports-annotation"] on the alias, fulfilling the "deprecated alias" requirement. - Recommended and strict configs (configs.recommended and configs.strict) only include the core rules and do not mention either prefer-* rule (confirmed by tests), so this rule is opt-in and disabled by default (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, acceptance criterion "Configurable Enforcement").,Documentation for this story’s rule: docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md - Titled "prefer-supports-annotation" and clearly describes: * The rule as an optional migration aid from @story/@req to @supports. * The canonical rule key "traceability/prefer-supports-annotation" and deprecated alias "traceability/prefer-implements-annotation" (Rule Naming acceptance criterion, REQ-RULE-NAME). * Behavior for legacy @story + @req blocks, mixed usage, multi-story, and ignored cases, matching the Implementation Notes and Acceptance Criteria in the story. * Configuration examples showing how to set severities off/warn/error for prefer-supports-annotation and the alias (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, acceptance criteria "Optional Warning" and "Configurable Enforcement"). * Auto-fix examples closely matching those given in the story (single-story and multi-req variants), verifying that documentation for migration and opt-in configuration exists (acceptance criterion "Documentation").,User-facing migration guide: user-docs/migration-guide.md - Contains section "Optional prefer-supports-annotation migration rule" which: * Describes the purpose of prefer-supports-annotation. * States that the legacy key traceability/prefer-implements-annotation remains as a deprecated alias. * Clarifies that the rule is disabled by default and not part of presets. * Shows example ESLint flat config enabling "traceability/prefer-supports-annotation": "warn". * Explains conservative auto-fix behavior, multi-story and mixed-annotation handling, and when comments are ignored. - Aligns with the story’s "Documentation" acceptance criterion (migration guide, auto-fix examples, opt-in configuration).,Test execution: npm test -- --verbose - Jest run includes suite: "prefer-supports-annotation / prefer-implements-annotation aliasing (Story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS)" and "prefer-implements-annotation configuration severity (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY)". - All tests in tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts passed, including those for: * [REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION] valid legacy and supports-only comments. * [REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING], [REQ-AUTO-FIX], [REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX], [REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT]. * Configuration severity behavior and disabled-by-default semantics. - Overall Jest summary: 48 of 49 test suites passed, 356 tests passed, 0 failures. The suite for this story’s rule is explicitly among the passing suites, confirming behavior works under test conditions.
traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements for story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are implemented and verified: - The rule is exposed under the canonical name traceability/prefer-supports-annotation, with traceability/prefer-implements-annotation wired as a deprecated alias in src/index.ts and documented in docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md and user-docs/migration-guide.md (REQ-RULE-NAME, Rule Naming AC). - The rule emits configurable recommendations when @story + @req appear together, while remaining disabled by default and absent from built-in presets (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, Optional Warning and Configurable Enforcement ACs). - Auto-fix logic exists, is intentionally conservative, and is exercised by tests covering single-story, single-req and multi-req cases, plus non-fixable complex patterns (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT, related ACs Auto-fix Support, Single Story Conversion, Preserve Order, Quality Standards). - Multi-story and mixed-annotation patterns are detected and reported with appropriate messages and without auto-fix (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT, Multi-story Detection AC). - Backward compatibility is preserved: legacy @story/@req remain valid when the rule is off, and even when enabled the rule ignores comments without both tags, while core validation rules are unchanged (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION, Both Formats Valid AC). - Documentation includes a dedicated rule doc and a user-facing migration guide with auto-fix examples and opt-in configuration (Documentation AC).
All relevant tests for this story pass in the current test run, providing concrete evidence that the implementation satisfies the story’s requirements.
